mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the rule that unauthenticated operations are rejected; the injected fact then forces an existing Operation atom to be both Unauthenticated and Successful, which AuthRequiredEverywhere claims is impossible.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthBypass { some op: Operation | op.role = Unauthenticated and op.outcome = Success }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the requirement that a successful DELETE produces a TaskDeletion log entry; the injection forces a successful DeleteTask op with no producesDeletion, directly contradicting the AuditCompleteness assertion.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MissingDeletionLog { some op: Operation | op.kind = DeleteTask and op.outcome = Success and no op.producesDeletion }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the constraint that a deletion log entry's deletedBy matches the operation's caller; the injection forces a misattributed log row to exist, which the assertion is designed to catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MisattributedDeletion { some op: Operation, td: TaskDeletion | op.producesDeletion = td and td.deletedBy != op.caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact lets two distinct Operations share the same TaskDeletion entry, simulating a mutated/re-attributed log row. The injection forces exactly that shared-origin scenario, breaking AppendOnly.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_SharedDeletionOrigin { some disj op1, op2: Operation | some op1.producesDeletion and op1.producesDeletion = op2.producesDeletion }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the closed-task PATCH guard; the injection then forces a successful PATCH on a Done task that does not reopen it, which FR_011_ClosedTaskRule forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_ClosedTaskEdited { some op: Operation | op.kind = PatchTask and op.outcome = Success and op.preStatus = Done and (no op.intendedNewStatus or op.intendedNewStatus = Done) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing this fact removes the rule that an invalid payload must lead to rejection; the injection forces an Operation with payloadValid=False and outcome=Success, the exact counterexample ValidationBeforeMutation is meant to rule out.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_InvalidPayloadAccepted { some op: Operation | op.payloadValid = False and op.outcome = Success }
